title: aidd library standard
description: The YAML front matter of one opinionated standard in aidd's library (`standards/<group>/<topic>.md`): one choice a pack or practice skill leaves open, with its why, its tool and checked version, and the tests that enforce it. `aidd standard add` copies the file into a project. Industry standards live only in the registry (`schemas/industry-standards.json`), never here.

id.description: Stable id, `<group>/<topic>`, such as `python/ruff-lint-format`. It matches the file's path under `standards/`. A renamed id stays in `schemas/retired-names.json`, as a `standard_id` row.

type.description: Always `opinionated`: a choice a team commits to. An industry standard lives in the registry and is only waived per project.

fills.description: The open choices it answers, each `<pack or skill>:<choice>`, such as `ci-pipeline:linter`. Required for a library standard, so it cannot overlap a pack.

default.description: Whether it is aidd's default for each choice it fills, in its ecosystem. The library may hold several options for one choice; exactly one active option per choice and ecosystem is the default. A project adopts one of them.

implements.description: The pack or skill rule it puts to work, `<pack or skill>:<rule>`, such as `product-defaults:dev_basics`. It links the rule and never restates it.

roles.description: aidd-team roles that read it before their step, or `*` for every role.

when_changed.description: Load it, and run its tests, only for a change that touches one of these paths.

why.description: Why this option, in one or two sentences.

maturity.description: Established tools are checked yearly; emerging ones every 90 days.

tool.description: The tool it chooses, and where its releases are published. The weekly standards check reads that feed and flags a newer major than `checked_version`. It reads stable releases only and, for `version_policy: latest_lts`, the newest LTS release where the feed marks one.

name.description: The tool's name, such as `ruff`. One library standard owns each tool.

registry.description: The release feed: PyPI, npm, crates.io, Maven Central, NuGet, the Go module proxy, or GitHub releases for a package; for a language toolchain, its official feed: go.dev, nodejs.org, the .NET release index, Adoptium, or python.org.

package.description: The name in that feed: a package, `group:artifact` on Maven Central, a module path on the Go proxy, or `owner/repo` on GitHub. A toolchain feed takes one fixed name: `go`, `node`, `sdk` or `runtime` (.NET), `temurin`, or `cpython`. Its form is checked per feed, so it can only name a package there.

version_policy.description: Which version a project uses. A project takes it through its own lockfile, which its updater moves, so the library names no version for it. `pinned` keeps one version for good, for a reason the body gives.

checked_version.description: The newest release read at the source on the `checked` day, so the weekly standards check can flag a newer major. Never typed from memory, and never a version a project must use.

checked.description: The day an agent last checked the standard: it read `checked_version` at the tool's release feed, or the standard's claim at its source, and found the choice still the right one for its slot. It needs a `citation`. Due again after a year when established, after 90 days when emerging.

checked_by.description: Who read `citation.url` on the `checked` day: `agent:<harness>/<model>` for the agent that checked it, the usual case, or a person's identity (`@login` or `email:<address>`). An agent checks every entry; the field records which one.

citation.description: The official page, `url`, where `checked_version` or the standard's claim was read on the `checked` day, and the `quote` read there, copied exactly, so the date is never a bare assertion. Required with `checked`.

alternatives.description: Other valid options for the same choice, by name. A company picks one through `standards_policy.replace`.

status.description: `deprecated`: kept so projects that copied it hear about it; `replaced_by` names the successor.

replaced_by.description: The library standard that replaces a deprecated one.

enforced_by.description: `tests` templates. `aidd standard add` writes each one, so `aidd test` runs it on every change its `when_changed` matches.

lock_command.description: The command that adds the dev tools its tests run to the project's lock, such as `[uv, add, --dev, ruff]` or `[go, get, -tool, golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck]`. `aidd standard add` prints it, so the tests run on the first day. A framework the tests also run, such as Django or Next.js, is the app's own dependency, so it names none.

choice_ref.description: An open choice, `<pack or skill>:<choice id>`, such as `ci-pipeline:linter`.
